topic: Resolve initiative edge drift surfaced by swarm-manager overview
description: swarm-manager overview consistency reports 2 missing_explicit edges (child items cross an initiative boundary with no declared parent-initiative dependency) and ~12 possibly_stale edges (declared initiative dependency has no supporting child dependency). Hygiene, not blockers, but unresolved drift erodes trust in the sequencing signal portfolio-manager relies on. Missing_explicit: (1) contribution-outbound-v1-bug-reports -> contribution-settings via execute/contribution-submitter-bug-report, (2) desktop-runtime-interop -> emulator-platform via execute/desktop-ecosystem-interop-regression-coverage. Possibly_stale set spans agent-inbox-unified-retrieval, agent-sandbox-audit-foundation, contribution-inbound-triage, contribution-outbound-extensions, contribution-verification-isolated, decision-visual-grounding-propagation, desktop-release-governance, director-dashboard-gap-workflow, ecosystem-intelligence-loop, and others.

options.label: Add the two missing_explicit edges; keep possibly_stale as-is
options.rationale: Missing edges are real dependencies the graph is hiding. Possibly_stale often reflects architectural (not item-level) dependencies that are legitimately declared only at the initiative level. Minimum-churn fix.

options.label: Add missing + drop all possibly_stale
options.rationale: Treat the graph as strictly item-derived. Aggressive cleanup; risks losing coarse-grained architectural dependencies that never had matching item edges.

options.label: Defer all edge cleanup
options.rationale: Accept drift; revisit when initiative-level dependency mutation tooling lands.

notes: Add the two missing_explicit edges; leave possibly_stale alone. Operator also endorsed a systemic follow-up: run the consistency check on every mutation that could affect edges (item create/edit/move/delete, initiative edit), surface drift delta on API/CLI/UI response with a suggested one-step fix, and add a vetted mark for legitimately architectural possibly_stale edges so they stop being repeat noise. topic: Tier-3 (hosted-cloud) positioning vs web-console headliner status
description: The 2026-04-25 vision walk surfaced a question: should web-console-readiness depend on a hosted-Vrooli cloud-tier prerequisite, since web-console's most compelling pitch (use it from your phone) requires Vrooli to run somewhere the customer can reach without self-hosting? Investigation confirmed docs/monetization/catalog/base/business.md positions web-console as already-deployable for self-hosters with a real but narrow audience. The decision is whether to (A) hard-reorder headliners and gate web-console-readiness on a Tier 3 prerequisite, (B) skip Tier 3 work entirely and keep self-host as the only path, or (C) keep web-console's headliner status accurate for self-hosters while adding Tier 3 as a parallel expansion that opens the larger phone-anywhere market.

options.label: Hard reorder — GCT becomes #1, web-console-readiness depends_on hosted-cloud-tier-foundation, catalog repositioned
options.rationale: Phone-anywhere is the load-bearing pitch; without it web-console is just a fancier terminal. Forces sequencing discipline.

options.label: No Tier 3 work — keep catalog as-is; phone-anywhere remains permanently aspirational
options.rationale: Self-host audience is enough; saves operational complexity of running customer instances.

options.label: Coexistence — keep catalog headliner status; create hosted-cloud-tier-foundation as Tier 3 expansion; no depends_on edge
options.rationale: Catalog framing is accurate for self-hosters; Tier 3 expands addressable market without invalidating Tier 1 pitch. Both audiences get served. Filed alongside this decision: initiative hosted-cloud-tier-foundation (priority 6, status active, foundation pattern).

notes: Operator selected coexistence at the moment of filing. Initiative hosted-cloud-tier-foundation is already active (priority 6, created same day). Web-console-readiness is unchanged — no depends_on edge, no catalog repositioning. Both pitches operate in parallel: Tier 1 self-host pitch as currently catalogued, Tier 3 hosted pitch as the new expansion path. Future telemetry on Tier 1 audience size may revisit this; not encoded today. See orchestration-summary.md on hosted-cloud-tier-foundation for the full reasoning chain.

decision: Propose new initiative: social-media-scheduler scenario buildout (marketing publish-pipeline domain)
rationale:
Surfaced at vision walk #4 (2026-04-27) Phase 8. The marketing-crew publishing infrastructure currently has no scenario home for domain-specific publish-pipeline operations; the workaround is operator-manual-edit of marketing-crew/shared/publish-log.jsonl. As publish volume scales (especially with the bookmark-intelligence-hub-rework-and-ideation initiative feeding more idea candidates into dev-log production), this becomes a real bottleneck.

Per the wrap-not-use principle, marketing-publishing is its own domain and should live in its own scenario, not be bolted onto prompt-manager (which stays scoped to generic team / coordination primitives). docs/marketing/ already references social-media-scheduler as a planned skill (in marketing-crew TEAM.md and the publisher member's responsibilities), implying a planned scenario behind it. This initiative proposal converts that intent into an actionable initiative.

PROPOSED SCOPE:

Core capabilities the scenario owns:
1. **Publish-log management.** Authoritative storage for marketing-crew/shared/publish-log.jsonl (or its successor schema). Includes the post_url roundtrip — operator manually posts to X (bot rules forbid auto-posting), then runs a CLI command (e.g., social-media-scheduler publish-log set-url --draft-id ID --url URL) to fill the URL back. Eliminates manual jsonl editing entirely. CLI ergonomics include set-url, mark-published, link-to-previous (for series chaining), and list / search across published artifacts.
2. **Series tracking.** First-class support for series_id, post_index_in_series, previous_post_url chaining (the schema designed in walk #4 first divergence). Drafters consume these from the publish-log when composing new posts in a series.
3. **Platform-specific posting workflows.** Per-platform operator-handoff flows: for X (manual paste, bot rules), the scenario produces a clipboard-ready message and waits for URL paste-back; for platforms with formal API access (LinkedIn, blog backends, YouTube via uploads), automated posting can be supported once each platform integration matures.
4. **Variant generation per platform.** Same draft adapted to platform constraints (X char limits, LinkedIn formatting, blog SEO conventions). The marketing-crew publisher member's existing scope.
5. **Scheduling.** Post-at-time queue. Operator queues drafts for specific times; scenario surfaces the at-time prompt and supports drift-handling (post-now-anyway, defer, cancel).
6. **Coverage tracking integration.** Publish-log entries automatically update per-SKU coverage state in marketing-crew/shared/coverage/. Today this is publisher-member responsibility done by hand; scenario automates.
7. **Cross-scenario integration with BIH (bookmark-intelligence-hub).** The new published-scenario-mentions.jsonl and published-improvements-log.jsonl files (designed in walk #4 first divergence) are populated by social-media-scheduler when posts ship, not by hand. This closes the publish-log-to-mentions loop.

Constraints (settled, not for re-debate):
- Wrap-not-use governs all platform integration. X / LinkedIn / Mastodon / Bluesky / YouTube / blogs all get scenario-wrapped via this scenario or via BAS / future scenarios where useful — never directly.
- Manual posting is the v0 path for X (and any platform with strict bot rules). Operator pastes URL back via CLI. Automated posting is platform-specific and gated on each platform's terms permitting it.
- Identity / permissioning comes from agent-manager when agents call this scenario (not built today; design points at it).
- The scenario does NOT author content. Content authorship lives in marketing-crew advertisers (oss-advertiser, subscription-advertiser) and the publisher member who polishes drafts. social-media-scheduler is the publish-pipeline plumbing.

Out of scope:
- Content authorship (lives upstream in advertisers + publisher).
- Brand asset rendering or generation (lives in brand-manager scenario when shipped).
- Cross-platform analytics dashboards (might be a candidate add-on later; not v0).
- Generic team jsonl editing (rejected at walk #4 first divergence — different domain).

Cross-references:
- Vision walk #4 first divergence for the publish-log schema design; marketing-crew TEAM.md for the documented Publish-log shape.
- Marketing-crew TEAM.md for the publisher member responsibilities (currently does manually what this scenario will automate).
- BIH initiative bookmark-intelligence-hub-rework-and-ideation for the downstream consumer of publish-log data.
- Wrap-not-use principle in docs/concepts/ARCHITECTURE.md.

Recommendation: ACCEPT as initiative-proposal. Concrete scope, clear owner (marketing-crew + this new scenario), clear cross-team consumers, and downstream of work already shipped (publish-log shape) so it doesn't re-litigate settled design. Priority should be calibrated against business-bundle headliners — this is infrastructure that supports them, not itself a headliner. Suggested initial priority: 4 (medium-high) so it can be activated soon after the dev-log production cadence increases meaningfully (post-BIH-ideation-extraction-agent shipping).
notes: Deferred by operator during 2026-05-14 morning vision walk. Still a priority for marketing/publish pipeline, but revisit after audio-tools extraction, Swarm Manager integration, and initial GCT enhancements have progressed.

decision:
[initiative-readiness] Workshop-prioritize foundation initiatives with description-only scope

A) Promote design-language-foundation to the next workshop-authoring priority; hold hosted-cloud-tier-foundation and web-console-readiness until their prerequisites mature [RECOMMENDED] — design-language-foundation is priority 7, operator-declared top of the three infrastructure initiatives, and still has 0 member items despite concrete known gaps. hosted-cloud-tier-foundation is priority 6 but lower urgency and tied to pricing / hosted-tier research. web-console-readiness is priority 7 but explicitly gated on continuous-audio-platform, so workshop hardening now would risk shaping work before the audio layer stabilizes.

B) Workshop all three foundation initiatives now — Converts description-level gaps into items across design-language-foundation, hosted-cloud-tier-foundation, and web-console-readiness. Higher throughput on planning, but likely creates more pending scope while execution throughput is currently stalled.

C) Hold all three — Accept 0/0 and 0/1 rollups for now; revisit after execution velocity recovers or continuous-audio-platform moves.
rationale: Portfolio evidence from 2026-05-14 heartbeat: active initiatives remain 58; throughput dropped to 0 completed in 7d / 37 in 30d, with 4 created in 7d / 55 in 30d. The three infrastructure initiatives called out in the previous handoff remain under-authored: design-language-foundation is active priority 7 with 0/0 members and workshop-ready known gaps; hosted-cloud-tier-foundation is active priority 6 with 0/0 members and workshop-ready known gaps; web-console-readiness is active priority 7 with only execute/web-console-tts-code-tick-handling and is explicitly gated on continuous-audio-platform. This proposal is intentionally bounded to workshop prioritization; it does not create backlog items or mutate initiative metadata without approval.

decision:
[initiative-readiness] Prioritize GCT QA unblockers before expanding dependent GCT work

A) Promote and run the two GCT QA unblockers first [RECOMMENDED] — Treat fix/qa-git-control-tower-tests-playbook-schema-20260515 and execute/qa-git-control-tower-code-quality-20260408 as immediate GCT-readiness prerequisites. Raise their effective priority/queue order ahead of new GCT feature execution until the playbook schema passes and the code-quality item is retried or replaced by a successful equivalent. This unblocks git-control-tower-ai-provenance, commit-linking, GitHub integration, merge/conflicts, pre-commit security, and release-pipeline members that currently depend on one or both items.

B) Continue feature sequencing as-is — Leave the QA unblockers at their current backlog statuses/priorities and let normal queue selection discover them. Risk: dependent GCT initiatives continue to show flat 0/N progress while prerequisites sit as ordinary backlog items.

C) Split only the playbook schema fix forward — Promote fix/qa-git-control-tower-tests-playbook-schema-20260515 because it is small and fresh, but leave the failed code-quality item deferred. Lower immediate scope, but several GCT items still remain gated on the failed code-quality prerequisite.
rationale: Portfolio evidence from 2026-05-15 heartbeat: GCT cluster remains flat (AI provenance 0/2, commit-linking 0/3, GitHub integration 0/5, merge/conflicts 0/4, release pipeline 0/2, pre-commit security 1/5). The new fix/qa-git-control-tower-tests-playbook-schema-20260515 item is backlog priority 4 but now appears as a dependency across GCT members; execute/qa-git-control-tower-code-quality-20260408 remains failed priority 2 and is also a dependency across commit-linking, GitHub integration, merge/conflicts, release pipeline, and pre-commit security. Throughput remains 0 completed in 7d while created items rose 18/7d, so adding more dependent work is less useful than explicitly prioritizing the shared unblockers.
